title: Will DNC Services Corp / Democratic National Committee report more than $26M in cash on hand at the end of Q3? Above $26M
rules: If DNC Services Corp / Democratic National Committee's cash on hand is above $26 million as of September 30, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: This market resolves based on the official filing data released by the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Only the first official or non-preliminary release of the relevant statistic will be used to resolve the market, and subsequent revisions, corrections, or updates will not affect resolution.

blind.reasoning: FEC filings show the DNC had $16.9M cash on hand at Aug. 31, 2026, against $17.6M in debt, and its cash has stayed between about $14M and $17M all year. Strong summer fundraising (over $14M in July-August) barely moved the balance because spending kept pace. Topping $26M would take a net gain of more than $9M in September, the heaviest spending month before a midterm, which almost never happens without a one-off windfall or new borrowing.
blind.falsifier: The DNC's September monthly FEC report (filed around Oct. 20) shows cash on hand above $26M, for example because of a very large transfer from joint fundraising committees, a major donor surge, or new loan money still in the account on Sept. 30.

final.reasoning: The 21% midpoint likely reflects a thin market or speculation rather than any reported September windfall. Cash stood at $16.9M on Aug. 31 and has ranged $14-17M all year, so topping $26M at Sept. 30 would take an unprecedented one-month gain. I raised my estimate slightly to 7% for news I couldn't check, but that is still far below the market.
